issue: Benchmark name in figure label appears wrong: the capability-screen box reads "Capability MLU/GSM8K". The standard benchmark is MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding); "MLU" is not a recognized benchmark name.
evidence: Rendered page 241, lower-left orange box of Fig 14.1: literal text "Capability MLU/GSM8K". GSM8K is spelled correctly, making a deliberate abbreviation of MMLU unlikely.
acceptance_test: Figure box reads "MMLU/GSM8K" and matches whatever benchmark name the surrounding prose (§14 Architecture Consequence / model-selection chapters) uses; global grep confirms a single spelling of MMLU throughout manuscript and figures.

issue: Visual verdict encoding contradicts the caption's scope. The figure's ④ OUTCOME box labels (a) and (b) as "SURVIVORS" in a green (pass-style) box and marks only (c) as "✗ GATED (c) pending Ch. 14", while the caption states all three are "conditional candidates, each with its own open validation gate (not a settled verdict)" and "each must measure its gate (throughput for a/b, quality for c)". A reader inspecting the figure alone will infer that (a) and (b) have cleared validation. Note also the terminology collision: figure "GATED" = blocked, caption "open gate" = not yet measured.
evidence: Fig 12.1 outcome row: green box "④ OUTCOME / SURVIVORS (a)·(b) / each needs a ~5-host prefill pool" vs red hatched box "✗ GATED / (c) pending Ch. 14"; caption on same page: "three conditional candidates, each with its own open validation gate (not a settled verdict)". Consistent with Table 12-1 on PDF p.222, where (b)'s verdict is "conditional finalist — ✗" and (c)'s is "gated, not a finalist".
acceptance_test: Outcome box conveys provisionality for (a) and (b) as well (e.g., relabel "SURVIVORS" to "PROVISIONAL OUTCOME" or add an explicit "gates still open" annotation on (a)/(b)), so the figure's visual semantics match the caption's "not a settled verdict" for all three candidates.

issue: P/D-specific terminology applied to a non-disaggregated candidate: the OUTCOME box says survivors "(a)·(b) each needs a ~5-host prefill pool", but candidate (a) is "8×H100 + prefix cache" with no disaggregation, so it has no separate prefill pool — it needs ~5 identical hosts sized by the canonical prefill demand (92K tok/s ÷ ~19.8K/host ≈ 4.65, per PDF p.222). Using "prefill pool" for both blurs the very P/D distinction the chapter is teaching.
evidence: Fig 12.1 CANDIDATES box: "(a) 8×H100 + prefix cache · (b) P/D 2-pool"; OUTCOME box: "each needs a ~5-host prefill pool". PDF p.222 row (b) uses "prefill pool" correctly in the disaggregated context ("prefill pool must scale to ~5 hosts").
acceptance_test: Outcome text distinguishes the two: e.g., "(a) ≈5 identical hosts at the canonical prefill rate; (b) a ~5-host prefill pool plus a decode pool", or the caption defines "prefil pool" here as shorthand for "hosts sized by prefill demand".

figure: Figure 15.2(b) (Relative decode goodput vs decode batch size)
issue: Caption and figure disagree about whether saturation is depicted. Caption: batching raises decode goodput "rising until HBM bandwidth saturates"; the drawn curve rises monotonically to the right edge with no plateau, and the in-figure annotation explicitly says "no hard plateau: goodput still rises". The caption implies a saturation point the figure does not show (and the annotation denies within the plotted range).
evidence: Fig 15.2 caption: "batching raises decode goodput (right: decode goodput vs batch size, arbitrary goodput units, rising until HBM bandwidth saturates)"; in-figure red annotation: "diminishing gains past ~b16 (no hard plateau): goodput still rises; tail latency keeps rising"; blue curve shows no flattening before the right axis edge.
acceptance_test: Caption reworded to match the drawn behavior (e.g., "rising with diminishing gains as bandwidth headroom shrinks; saturation is workload-dependent"), or the curve/annotation extended to show the bandwidth-saturation regime it names.

figure: Figure 15.2(a) (Prefill FLOPs/req vs avg prefix reuse)
issue: The with-cache curve's floor encodes an unstated assumption. The green curve falls from 100% at reuse 1 to only ~60–65% at reuse ≈50, which implies the reusable shared prefix is only ~35–40% of the prompt (floor = 1 − f_shared; 0.60 ⇒ f ≈ 0.40). Neither axis label, legend, nor caption states the shared-prefix fraction, so a reader cannot tell what drives the asymptote and may wrongly conclude prefix caching caps savings near 40% regardless of prefix size.
evidence: Rendered panel (a): y-axis "Prefill FLOPs / req (% of no-cache)", x-axis "Avg prefix reuse" (log, 1→~50); green "with prefix cache" series terminates around 60–65 at the rightmost point; caption scope is "[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]" but the assumption itself (shared-prefix fraction) is not named.
acceptance_test: Caption or an in-figure note states the assumed shared-prefix fraction (e.g., "assumes ~40% of each prompt is the shared prefix; floor = 1 − f_shared"), or the curve is redrawn for a stated f so the floor is derivable by the reader.

figure: Figure 15.1 (FlashAttention: the same math, far less HBM traffic)
issue: The figure's emphatic claim "same Q·Kᵀ·V math and same result" is stronger than the caption on the same page, which correctly caveats that tiled accumulation "can differ in the last bits under finite precision — a numerical-equivalence, not a bit-identical, claim". A reader who takes the figure's bold line at face value (e.g., quoting it in a design doc) gets an overstrong equivalence claim.
evidence: In-figure bold line: "same Q·Kᵀ·V math and same result — the gain is fewer HBM round-trips, not cheaper attention"; caption, same page: "results are equivalent in exact arithmetic but can differ in the last bits under finite precision".
acceptance_test: Figure line softened to match the caption's scope, e.g., "same Q·Kᵀ·V math, same result (up to floating-point ordering)" or "same attention target", so figure-alone reading cannot imply bit-identical outputs.

issue: Tight clearance in panel (b): the multi-line red annotation ("diminishing gains past ~b16 … tail latency keeps rising") occupies the upper-left plot area through roughly x≈16–30, the same region traversed by the rising blue goodput curve and the red dashed b≈16 marker. At 150 dpi the curve/marker appear to pass within a few points of the annotation's lower lines; possible touch or crossing cannot be excluded at this resolution.
evidence: Rendered panel (b): annotation block spans ~y=60–95 across ~x=2–30; blue curve passes y≈65 near x≈16 and y≈78 near x≈28; dashed vertical marker at x≈16 spans the full panel height through the annotation band.
